name: ai-memory
description: Solution for long term memory for agent coding CLIs and to facilitate handoff between different agent vendors
one_liner: A shared notebook for AI coding assistants — so when you switch from one AI tool to another, or come back the next day, it remembers what you were doing and why, instead of making you re-explain everything.
buyer: An engineering team lead whose developers use different AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) and keep losing context when they switch between them or between machines.
business_use_cases: A dev team runs a shared ai-memory server so a developer who starts a task in Claude Code and finishes it in Codex doesn't have to re-explain the architecture.
A freelance developer keeps per-client memory servers so returning to a client's project after weeks away doesn't cost an hour of re-orientation.
A dev agency onboarding a new hire points them at the project's memory server instead of writing a fresh onboarding doc for every AI session.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a hosted, managed version of the memory server for teams who don't want to run their own homelab box.
Consulting: set up and configure a team's shared memory server and cross-project profile as a one-time engagement.

steal_this: Spin up a hosted, zero-setup version of the memory server aimed at small dev teams, charged per seat, so they skip the homelab/self-hosting step entirely.
